examDifficulty.heading: Is the Industries CPQ Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This page reviews Industries CPQ development, including product configuration, pricing, orders and decomposition into fulfillment work.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Scenario-based choices: expect questions that test when to use Industries CPQ, Communications Cloud, or Media Cloud.
Hands-on context matters: candidates who have configured or supported Industries CPQ in a real org are better prepared than candidates who only memorize notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use the published objectives to review product modeling, rules, pricing, order handling and integrations. For each practice scenario, explain why the chosen configuration works and where custom code is actually needed.

examFormat.heading: Industries CPQ Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The Industries CPQ Developer exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios ask how to model a configurable offer, calculate its price, or carry an order into fulfillment.
bestWayToPass: Start with the product model: Learn how Product Specifications, Product Offerings, Bundles, and attributes define what a customer can buy.
Apply configuration rules: Use attribute and context rules to allow valid choices and make products available for the right account, location, or existing service.
Use Apex only for gaps: Build custom code when declarative rules cannot meet the requirement, and keep the extension within the Industries CPQ framework.
Test the full configuration: Check bundles, dependencies, rule order, and the final order payload with realistic customer and product combinations.

certificationCard.description: This page covers Industries CPQ solution development for configurable products and services, including catalog structure, rules, pricing and order processing.

keyConcepts.h2: Industries CPQ Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Product Catalog and Configuration
blocks.body: Model the commercial offer and its selectable characteristics. Configuration rules guide valid choices while the customer or seller builds the offer.

blocks.heading: Pricing
blocks.body: Separate base prices, adjustments and promotions in the pricing design. Use the appropriate pricing records or procedures to calculate the result from product choices.

blocks.heading: Quote and Order Flow
blocks.body: Follow the transaction from product selection through quote and order. Decomposition turns the customer-facing purchase into the work needed by downstream systems.

blocks.heading: APIs and Integration
blocks.body: Use the supported integration interfaces for catalog, configuration and order tasks. Plan for authentication, errors, retries and clear status when another system is unavailable.

blocks.heading: Declarative and Custom Logic
blocks.body: Start with configuration rules and supported declarative tools. Add Apex or other custom logic when the requirement cannot be met cleanly with standard configuration.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Industries CPQ Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Follow the product from selection through configuration, pricing, order submission and fulfillment.

blocks.heading: Model the offer first
blocks.body: Identify the product, its attributes and the rules that make combinations valid.

blocks.heading: Trace the price
blocks.body: Check which values affect price and where each adjustment enters the calculation.

blocks.heading: Follow decomposition
blocks.body: Confirm how the commercial order becomes fulfillment items and how failures can be reviewed or resumed.

blocks.heading: Prefer maintainable extensions
blocks.body: Use declarative features where they fit; isolate custom code and provide tests and error handling.

sampleQuestions.question: A buyer selects a service option that changes which other options are valid. How should the product be modeled?
options: A configurable product with attributes and rules
A separate product record for every possible combination
A text note where sales staff list selections
A post-order check that rejects combinations
sampleQuestions.explanation: Configuration attributes represent the choices, and rules can guide or restrict combinations while the offer is being configured.
whyWrong: A separate product record for every possible combination is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A configurable product with attributes and rules.
A text note where sales staff list selections is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A configurable product with attributes and rules.
A post-order check that rejects combinations is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A configurable product with attributes and rules.
